analysis.evidence: אֵת כָּל־הָרְכֻשׁ marks all the possessions as the direct object. The verse repeats the verb as הֵשִׁיב when it says that Abram also brought back Lot and his possessions.
analysis.morphology: The conjunction וַ introduces a Hiphil wayyiqtol, third person masculine singular, with Abram as the subject.

analysis.evidence: אֵת introduces כָּל הָרְכֻשׁ, “all the possessions,” as the definite direct object of וַיָּשֶׁב, “he brought back.”
analysis.morphology: Hebrew direct-object marker with no prefix or suffix.

analysis.evidence: In וַיָּשֶׁב אֵת כָּל הָרְכֻשׁ, “he brought back all the property,” כָּל refers to the full amount of property recovered.
analysis.morphology: Masculine singular noun in the construct state, with הָרְכֻשׁ as its complement.

draft.change: Add the root רכש and its noun רְכוּשׁ for acquired possessions. The source’s personal-name gloss does not fit this occurrence.
draft.definition: Property or goods that someone owns, taken collectively.
draft.evidence: Genesis 12:5 pairs רְכוּשָׁם, “their possessions,” with רָכָשׁוּ, “they had acquired.”

analysis.evidence: Abram brought back אֵת כָּל הָרְכֻשׁ, “all the possessions.” The same noun recurs in וּרְכֻשׁוֹ, “and his possessions,” referring specifically to Lot’s property.
analysis.morphology: The definite article הָ precedes a masculine singular absolute noun used collectively.

analysis.evidence: Carried forward: this word and its source tagging were reviewed identically at 69127:12, 68869:0, 67076:5.
analysis.morphology: The prefixed conjunction וְ means “and.” The additive particle גַם means “also” and places the focus on אֶת הָאֱמֹרִי.
Hebrew direct-object particle with no prefix or suffix.
